briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development of the past 24 hours was the attempted terror attack on Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, where an Omani co-pilot allegedly stabbed the Indian captain and attempted to crash the plane, leading to an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. This incident, thwarted by passenger and crew intervention, has been declared a "jihadist terrorist attack" by Israel, with investigations ongoing into potential Iranian involvement. Concurrently, the United States announced the final withdrawal of its forces from Iraq after over two decades, prompting celebrations in Baghdad amidst regional concerns over a power vacuum.

IRAN
US President Donald Trump stated that the conflict with Iran would end "very soon," claiming that Iran's military (navy, air force, air defence) is "gone" and its economy "destroyed" with inflation over 300%. He claimed the US has been at war with Iran for six months, losing 18 personnel compared to Iran's 4,500. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed UK PM Andy Burnham's claims linking Iran to the RAF Fairford incident, telling him he was "barking up the wrong tree" and suggesting the release of alleged terrorists by the UK "clarifies everything." Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) Secretary Major General Mohsen Rezaei warned the UAE that hosting Israeli PM Netanyahu would bring no security and fuel regional tensions, telling them to "cease issuing baseless claims regarding the Iranian islands." IRGC advisor Blali stated that Iran would fire "as many missiles as needed to deter the enemy." President Pezeshkian highlighted Iran's strong maritime presence in the Strait of Hormuz for keeping "vital national lifelines moving." Channel 14 (Israel) reported missile launches from near Shiraz, Fars province, with unspecified targets, though an Iranian military source denied any missile launch from Shiraz or attack on an airbase in Jordan. There were reports of explosions in southeastern Iran, but no further details. Domestically, two protesters, Ali Hemmati and Majid Nikandish, were executed in Mashhad for their alleged involvement in the December 2025 protests. Concerns were raised by Al Jazeera about Iranians hoarding food and medicine due to fears of shortages from potential war. Russian state nuclear company Rosatom expressed readiness to share nuclear expertise with global partners.

ISRAEL
Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing at Tabuk Airport, Saudi Arabia, after the Omani co-pilot allegedly stabbed the Indian captain and attempted to crash the aircraft. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz declared the incident a "jihadist terrorist attack attempt," intended to crash the plane with all 180 passengers. PM Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the co-pilot was arrested and is being interrogated by Saudi authorities, praising the "heroes" who prevented a "major catastrophe." He stated that the Mossad is leading the investigation, with Shin Bet assisting. US Ambassador Mike Huckaby praised the "bravery of Israelis" for preventing the disaster. Flydubai suspended flights to Israel until the investigation is complete. Israeli Transportation Minister Miri Regev requested Shin Bet to halt all Flydubai flights. El Al and Arkia are preparing to resume/increase flights on the Tel Aviv-Dubai route in November, with El Al planning at least two daily flights. Netanyahu discussed aircraft security with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, who agreed to "security demands" allowing Israeli airlines to operate more flights. An Israeli official suggested the attacker aimed to destabilize the Abraham Accords. Earlier warnings from Shin Bet head Zini about "severe security problems on flights from the Emirates to Israel" were reported. One passenger, a 51-year-old man, was hospitalized in good condition with upper body trauma after the rescue flight landed at Ben Gurion International Airport, where Netanyahu and Minister Regev greeted the passengers. Israeli Air Force F-15 fighter jets escorted the rescue flight into Israeli airspace. President Isaac Herzog, during a visit to the Judea and Samaria Division, condemned "serious phenomena of nationalist crime," stating it harms Israel's reputation and settlement, urging political leadership to provide tools to stop it. An Israeli citizen was reported murdered in Koh Phangan, Thailand. A 22-year-old man was severely injured in a shooting in Ibtin, south of Kiryat Ata. A 21-year-old electric scooter rider and a 10-year-old girl were seriously injured in separate incidents in Acre. A 31-year-old cyclist was severely injured in Rehovot.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Palestinian media reported at least four (later five) dead, including Ammar al-Sharfi (brother of Al Jazeera reporter Moamen al-Sharfi), in an Israeli airstrike targeting a minibus in Tel al-Hawa neighborhood, Gaza City. Hamas threatened that this was a "dangerous development" that undermined the ceasefire agreement and held Israel responsible for consequences. Another strike was reported near Aqila Hotel, north of Khan Yunis. A Palestinian child was reportedly injured in an Israeli drone strike on Al-Qarara, southern Gaza. A mass funeral was held in Gaza City for over 105 Palestinians whose remains were recovered from rubble. In the West Bank, 9 suspects from the same family in Judea and Samaria were arrested for burglaries in Beit Shemesh. Two of three arrestees from unrest in Jalud were released to house arrest despite police appeals, drawing criticism from the security establishment.

LEBANON
IDF Golani forces completed 7 months of operations in southern Lebanon, during which rockets, explosives, explosive drones, and terror infrastructure were destroyed, and are now withdrawing for refreshment. Lebanese media reported Israeli airstrikes and artillery fire targeting areas near Baraashit, Beit Yahoun, Al-Mansouri, and Houla in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah released a message vowing to continue fighting, following the death of its leader Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah (implied, though the source implies it's a message to Nasrallah).

SYRIA & IRAQ
The US officially announced the final withdrawal of US-led coalition forces from Iraq, ending over two decades of military presence. President Trump stated he had "a choice to stay or to leave" and decided it was "time for America to go home," calling it a "great day for America" and a "decisive victory over ISIS." Iraqi resistance groups, including Kata'ib Hezbollah, celebrated the withdrawal, vowing to retain their weapons to confront any American or Israeli threat and insisting decisions are now solely for Iraqi state institutions. Kata'ib Hezbollah Secretary-General Abu Hussein al-Hamidawi said the resistance was victorious and would impose its conditions on the enemy, stating their weapons would remain to defend Iraq. Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi (whom Trump took credit for electing) affirmed that security and military decisions are now exclusively held by Iraqi government entities. Iraqis celebrated in Baghdad's Tahrir Square and Palestine Street, with military parades. Kurdistan Regional Government Prime Minister Masrour Barzani reportedly views the US withdrawal as "shameful" and expressed concerns about increased vulnerability to Iran. In Syria, an explosion at a gas pipeline supplying the Tishreen Thermal Power Plant near Damascus International Airport caused three power plants to go offline. Unidentified armed individuals attacked a bus in rural Hama, killing at least 7 and injuring 4. In Iraq, reports indicated drone attacks on the Azadi camp in Koya, Erbil province, targeting Iranian opposition parties. An American female spy, TARA KAY DEROSSETT, was reportedly arrested in Tahrir Square, Baghdad, while filming Popular Mobilization Forces officials.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia played a critical role in the Flydubai incident, allowing the emergency landing at Tabuk Airport and arresting the Omani co-pilot. Saudi authorities provided assistance and hospitality to the Israeli passengers before they were transferred to a rescue flight. Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport experienced multiple air traffic halts within the week, ordering aircraft into holding patterns. Saudi warplanes carried out 51 airstrikes in Yemen over the past 24 hours, targeting civilian communication networks and objects in the governorates of Marib, Saada, Hodeidah, Taiz, and Amran. Yemeni Houthi forces claimed to have targeted two main Saudi refineries and the Abqaiq processing facilities. Trump claimed the US had "almost complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz and that "more oil has exited the Strait of Hormuz in the last three days than at any time in history." However, Iran's IRGC claimed the US has lost its response capability as Iran maintains control of the Strait, and TankerTrackers reported that total crude oil exports from the Middle East increased by 36% to 17.92 million barrels per day, with 12.35 million bpd passing through Hormuz. A crude oil tanker was reportedly hit by an unknown projectile on its port side in the Strait of Hormuz on September 29, according to UKMTO. Qatar and Egypt discussed regional de-escalation, with Qatar emphasizing diplomatic efforts to ensure freedom of navigation in regional waters. Netanyahu told UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed that Iran might launch a regional attack "within weeks" and showed him new intelligence on Iran's nuclear program.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Flydubai Terror Attack Attempt:** Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv experienced a co-pilot stabbing the captain and attempting to crash the plane, deemed a "jihadist terrorist attack" by Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz, thwarted by passengers and crew, leading to an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
2.  **US Troop Withdrawal from Iraq:** President Donald Trump announced the final withdrawal of all US forces from Iraq, ending a 23-year military presence, which was met with celebrations by Iraqi resistance groups and the government in Baghdad.
3.  **UK Accusation Against Iran:** UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated "strong indications" suggest Iran's involvement in a recent security incident at RAF Fairford, a US-managed airbase in Britain.
4.  **Strait of Hormuz Incident:** A crude oil tanker was reportedly hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on September 29, amidst conflicting claims of control over the waterway by the US and Iran.
5.  **Gaza Airstrike and Casualties:** An Israeli airstrike on a minibus in Gaza City killed at least five Palestinians, including a journalist's brother, prompting threats from Hamas.
6.  **Syrian Infrastructure Attacks:** An explosion on a gas pipeline supplying the Tishreen Thermal Power Plant near Damascus knocked out three power plants, and a bus attack in rural Hama killed at least seven people.
7.  **Israeli Flight Security Measures:** Following the Flydubai incident, Flydubai suspended flights to Israel, while Israeli airlines El Al and Arkia announced preparations to resume/increase direct flights to Dubai with enhanced security.
8.  **Iranian Executions:** Two protesters, Ali Hemmati and Majid Nikandish, arrested during the December 2025 protests, were executed in Mashhad, Iran.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of a wider regional conflict is extremely high. The Flydubai incident, labelled a "jihadist terror attack" by Israel, with investigations into potential Iranian links, could serve as a significant flashpoint, potentially escalating the Israel-Iran conflict beyond direct military confrontations. Trump's bellicose rhetoric ("blow them up") against Iran, coupled with Iran's defensive posturing and claims of controlling the Strait of Hormuz, indicates a precarious balance. The US withdrawal from Iraq creates a power vacuum that could be exploited by Iranian-backed militias, increasing instability and proxy conflicts within Iraq and along its borders. Attacks in Syria (bus, power plant) and against opposition groups in Iraqi Kurdistan point to ongoing internal and cross-border tensions. The reported targeting of a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz suggests continued maritime insecurity. Netanyahu's warning to the UAE of imminent Iranian attacks "within weeks" underscores the immediate escalation risk.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** President Trump announced the withdrawal of US forces from Iraq, touting it as a "great day for America" and a "decisive victory over ISIS." He maintained a strong stance on Iran, claiming their military is "gone" and economy "destroyed," and hinting at imminent actions ("You will see things happening very soon"). He also took credit for the election of Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi. The Pentagon confirmed the end of Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq. CENTCOM redirected 125 commercial vessels by September 30. The State Department offered a reward of up to $15 million for information on senior IRGC Aerospace Force commanders. Axios reported that US-Iran diplomatic efforts through Qatari mediators made little progress.
**United Kingdom:** Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated there are "strong indications" of Iran's role in the RAF Fairford incident. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband expressed concern over the Flydubai incident and appreciated that the plane landed safely.
**European Union:** The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) recommended against flights in Jordanian airspace at all altitudes and extended flight suspensions in Iraqi, Lebanese, Jordanian, and Iranian airspace until mid-October 2026. The EU is reviewing its "Irini" naval mission in the Mediterranean to counter Russia's shadow fleet.
**Russia:** Threatened NATO with nuclear weapons if the alliance tried to cut off Kaliningrad. Its Defense Ministry claimed to have targeted a Ukrainian military cargo ship in the Black Sea.
**Saudi Arabia:** Facilitated the emergency landing of the Flydubai flight in Tabuk, arrested the Omani co-pilot, and provided assistance to passengers. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh experienced multiple air traffic halts. Saudi warplanes continued airstrikes in Yemen.
**UAE:** Agreed to Israeli security demands regarding flights following the Flydubai incident, allowing Israeli airlines to operate the route. President Mohammed bin Zayed spoke with Netanyahu regarding aircraft security.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are contradictions regarding the Flydubai incident: Israeli officials initially suspected the co-pilot acted alone, but later senior officials (e.g., Israel Katz) firmly declared it a "jihadist terror attack" with implied Iranian links, while the Mossad is leading the investigation into potential Iranian involvement. Flydubai itself stated the motive is unclear and under official investigation. There are also conflicting reports on missile launches from Iran; Israeli Channel 14 reported ballistic missile launches from Shiraz, which an Iranian military source explicitly denied. The claim of Mirhossein Mousavi's death is unconfirmed. Speculation about providing free, unfiltered internet to Iran (Amjad Taha) lacks verifiable basis. Trump's statements regarding the number of casualties in the "war with Iran" (18 US, 4500 Iranian) are unverified and differ from official reporting. The comparison of the Flydubai incident to "Israel's 9/11" or "July 1976" (Entebbe) is a propaganda indicator used to emphasize severity. The precise targets and full extent of damage from attacks in Erbil against Kurdish parties are not detailed in the provided messages. There's a reporting gap on the specific nature of the "Hezbollah message" (whether it's a general statement or related to a specific event/individual). The dispute between Netanyahu and Lapid over security briefings before the alleged "election attacks" highlights internal political tensions and potential politicization of intelligence.
